results.question: What is the mandatory threshold for filing a Currency Transaction Report (CTR)?
results.actualAnswer: Under Currency Transaction Reporting standards and federal law, cash transactions exceeding $10,000 conducted by or on behalf of one person in a single business day require mandatory filing of a Currency Transaction Report (CTR) [AML Transaction Monitoring Procedure, Section 2].

results.question: What constitutes structuring or smurfing under Scenario TM-RULE-101?
results.actualAnswer: Under AML Transaction Monitoring Procedure (Scenario TM-RULE-101), structuring is defined as multiple cash deposits or withdrawals conducted across branches or ATMs within a rolling 72-hour window where individual amounts range between $7,000 and $9,999 and total aggregated cash exceeds $10,000 [AML Transaction Monitoring Procedure, Section 2].

results.question: What equity ownership percentage triggers the requirement for Ultimate Beneficial Owner (UBO) identification?
results.actualAnswer: Pursuant to the FinCEN Customer Due Diligence (CDD) Rule and Bank Policy, beneficial ownership identification is required for every individual who directly or indirectly owns or controls 25% or more of the equity interests of a legal entity [KYC Verification Procedure, Section 3].

results.question: Within how many calendar days must a Suspicious Activity Report (SAR) be filed after a suspicious determination?
results.actualAnswer: Suspicious Activity Reports (SAR) must be filed with FinCEN or the national FIU no later than 30 calendar days from the date of initial alert review and suspicious determination (extended to 60 days if no suspect was initially identified) [AML Transaction Monitoring Procedure, Section 3].

results.question: Under AML-SOP-005 Section 2, what documents and verification methods are required for natural persons?
results.actualAnswer: Under AML-SOP-005 Section 2, natural persons require unexpired government photo identification verified via forensic MRZ/barcode scanning and facial liveness, proof of residential address dated within 90 calendar days (PO Boxes strictly prohibited), and Tax Identification Number (SSN/ITIN) [KYC Verification Procedure, Section 2].

results.question: How does the annual review cadence for High Risk customers in AML-POL-002 align with the incomplete KYC freeze in AML-SOP-005?

results.question: Explain how an alert escalated to a Level-2 Case under AML-SOP-001 transitions into the five-step investigation in AML-SOP-003.
results.actualAnswer: When an alert cannot be justified commercially under AML-SOP-001 Section 4, it is escalated to a Level-2 Case. AML-SOP-003 Section 3 then governs case execution through five sequential steps: Customer Profile Baseline (Step 1), Transaction Flow & Velocity Mapping (Step 2), Counterparty Verification (Step 3), Adverse Media Screening (Step 4), and Economic Rationality Evaluation (Step 5) [AML Transaction Monitoring Procedure, Section 4; Suspicious Activity Investigation Procedure, Section 3].

results.question: Synthesize the MLRO approval authority between the escalation hierarchy in AML-GUIDE-004 and the SAR filing mandate in AML-SOP-003.
results.actualAnswer: Under AML-GUIDE-004 Section 2 (Tier 3), the Chief AML Officer / MLRO holds sole authority to approve SAR filings, direct account freezing, and authorize law enforcement disclosures. AML-SOP-003 Section 1 and Section 5 operationalize this authority by defining FinCEN SAR filing directives and strictly prohibiting tipping-off under Section 6 [Transaction Escalation Guidelines, Section 2; Suspicious Activity Investigation Procedure, Section 1].

results.question: How do the mandatory high-risk customer designations in AML-POL-002 relate to the Source of Wealth verification in AML-SOP-005?
results.actualAnswer: AML-POL-002 Section 4 mandates automatic High-Risk status for PEPs, VASPs, and MSBs. Correspondingly, AML-SOP-005 Section 4 enforces mandatory Source of Wealth (SOW) corroboration (audited financial statements, tax filings, or title deeds) for all High-Risk customers, Private Banking clients, and PEPs [Customer Risk Assessment Policy, Section 4; KYC Verification Procedure, Section 4].

results.question: What is the threshold?
results.actualAnswer: Multiple statutory AML thresholds exist: the Currency Transaction Report (CTR) threshold is $10,000 cash; the TM-RULE-101 structuring threshold monitors transactions between $7,000 and $9,999; and the Ultimate Beneficial Owner (UBO) threshold is 25% or greater equity [AML Transaction Monitoring Procedure, Section 2; KYC Verification Procedure, Section 3].
